**Synopsis:**
Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, known for his aversion to forward guidance, offered markets a partial but meaningful signal at Jackson Hole — hinting a rate hike is likely at the September 15-16 FOMC meeting if inflation isn't clearly converging to the 2% target. His carefully calibrated remarks ("we have work to do") represent a modest rhetorical shift from his July press conference silence, enough to reprice futures markets toward tighter policy. Fellow Fed officials — Williams, Hammack, Goolsbee — have been more openly communicative, and former officials like Harker warn that words must be backed by action given inflation has run above target for nearly six years.
